brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Tallyline, the invoicing and cash-flow forecasting product in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: calm and trustworthy, friendly to freelancers, not the generic fintech blue-and-green. Web app only.

claim.notes: Runway ve Handover iki eskiz turunda elendi; Long t iki turda da kapıyı geçemedi (blind distinctiveness 4, memorability 4, brand-fit 5), bu yüzden export, install-assets ve galeri yapılmadı.

concepts.title: Handover
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a smiley face / u-umlaut; s2 two slabs and a dot, generic; s3 a percent sign (finance cliche); s4 a pause/volume glyph l.l; s5 Pac-Man or a puzzle piece; s6 a paperclip or a D with an equals sign; s7 the letter H/b in a block, a cut square monogram (stock-shape 79%); s8 a crop-tool icon / corner brackets. New s6-s8 drop the dot but land on a paperclip, a cut-square letter and a crop icon. Nothing I would bet reaches distinctiveness/memorability 7. No pick.

concepts.title: Runway
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 the dark-mode/contrast toggle icon (half-filled circle); s6 the same contrast icon in a squircle, generic diagonal split; s7 a medicine capsule broken open, or a padlock shackle. All three are one device (solid half + outline half + gap) applied to stock shapes, and it lands on UI icons every time. No pick. The booked-vs-forecast idea only works if the form itself is ownable; a fill-state split of a circle/tile/pill never will be.

concepts.title: Long t
readsAs: lowercase tl typed in a terminal followed by an underscore cursor and a period (tl_.)
two rising bars of unequal height on a shared base, a small bar chart
a cross on a plinth beside a post, like a grave marker. Unfortunate for this audience: a rising-bars finance chart, which the brief explicitly bans
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a lowercase t whose tail sweeps up into a tall stem, a one-stroke tl ligature (the hook it claims); s2 a broken plus sign or fishing hook, and the t split around the line is the initial-with-a-cut device, struck; s3 plain letters t...l with an ellipsis, typed text and loading, struck; s4 the letter H with a red bar, a different letter, struck. Keep s1: the single unbroken stroke that crosses the short stem and turns up into the l is the only gesture on all three boards that a stranger could remember. Fix: separate the clay dot from the stroke with a real gap (they merge in one colour now) or drop it; make the rising stem clearly taller than the t stem and keep the turn a round corner so it never reads as a checkmark or a J; keep the left lead-in long enough that the line, not the t, carries the mark; one stroke weight, round terminals.
